themes.title: The humanoid platform race
themes.description: Tesla ramped Optimus to several hundred units a week in Sep 2026 (10x its Q2 pace) but still can't get the robots to generalize past supervised factory tasks; Figure, Unitree, Agility and 150+ Chinese makers are racing the same problem from different angles.

themes.title: Reshoring keeps the automation base humming
themes.description: Fanuc, Yaskawa, ABB and Rockwell are riding a factory-reshoring cycle; Teradyne's Universal Robots unit just posted its first-ever $100M cobot quarter behind a new Gen 7 platform, and Fanuc is now shipping an AI welding agent built with Google's Gemini Enterprise.

themes.title: Warehouse automation is already profitable
themes.description: Symbotic turned GAAP-profitable last quarter on a ~$22.6B backlog — evidence that warehouse robotics, unlike humanoids, is already being paid for at scale by large retail and logistics customers.

themes.title: Da Vinci's monopoly is ending
themes.description: J&J's Ottava and Medtronic's Hugo are no longer paper competitors: Ottava got a flattering CNBC feature this month and Hugo keeps adding FDA-cleared indications, while Intuitive shares sit ~34% off their highs even after a fresh EU approval.

themes.title: Autonomy backlogs keep growing
themes.description: AeroVironment's backlog sits at a record $1.5B (1.4x book-to-bill) and Kratos grew revenue over 30% on its Valkyrie drone and laser lines — defense autonomy is one of the few robotics niches with immediate, funded demand.

themes.title: The humanoid supply chain is the safer bet
themes.description: Harmonic Drive's strain-wave reducers and Vishay Precision's sensors sit in the actuator bottleneck every humanoid maker has to solve, and MP Materials' rare-earth magnet capacity underwrites all of it — components get paid regardless of which humanoid brand wins.

bear_case.title: Humanoid valuations have outrun any plausible revenue
bear_case.description: Figure AI carries a ~$39B valuation on roughly 150 robots shipped in 2025; robotics VC funding is running near ~$56B in 2026 YTD against a market that's still mostly demos.

bear_case.title: Demos keep getting mistaken for autonomy
bear_case.description: Figure's Helix 2.5 and Skild's S1 both report large task-completion jumps this month, but the metrics track cumulative, human-assisted success — not full autonomy. If a demo isn't explicitly labelled autonomous, assume some teleoperation.

bear_case.title: Optimus's own maker has walked back its timeline twice
bear_case.description: Musk promised thousands of Optimus units doing 'useful work' by end of 2025; by January 2026 he admitted zero were. Output has since ramped to several hundred units a week, but generalization past supervised tasks hasn't.

bear_case.title: China's humanoid boom is drawing its own bubble warnings
bear_case.description: Chatham House and China's own NDRC have both flagged frothy valuations across the country's 150+ humanoid makers; Unitree's stock has given back most of its Shanghai IPO-day pop.

bear_case.title: Profitable names get cut anyway
bear_case.description: Symbotic turned GAAP-profitable with a ~$22.6B backlog and still saw two analyst target cuts in two weeks — a reminder sentiment and fundamentals can diverge in either direction, not just to the upside.

bear_case.title: Revenue today is still the boring parts of robotics
bear_case.description: Industrial automation, logistics automation and surgical robots generate real, recurring revenue now. Humanoids mostly don't yet — the investable robotics story and the humanoid hype story are not the same trade.

bear_case.title: Component suppliers carry customer-concentration risk of their own
bear_case.description: Vishay Precision's stock fell ~11% in a month on customer-concentration concerns even after a target upgrade tied to a humanoid design win — being 'picks and shovels' relocates single-customer risk rather than removing it.

bear_case.title: A crowded field guarantees a shakeout, not a winner
bear_case.description: 150+ companies are chasing humanoid robots globally. History suggests most of that capital doesn't survive to be recovered, even where the underlying technology thesis is directionally right.

catalysts.title: Tesla ramps Optimus output ~10x from Q2, to several hundred units/week
catalysts.description: Fremont's converted Model S/X line is now producing toward Tesla's stated 1,000+/week year-end target, but AI generalization and hand-assembly bottlenecks remain unresolved (Electrek).

catalysts.title: Symbotic highlighted as a robotics stock with paying customers
catalysts.description: Contrasted against pre-revenue humanoid bets given its GAAP profitability and ~$22.6B backlog (The Motley Fool).

catalysts.title: Unitree launches the G1+ with six hardware/software updates
catalysts.description: Comes as the stock continues to give back its Shanghai IPO-day pop amid both Chinese and Western bubble warnings.

catalysts.title: J&J's Ottava profiled as a credible da Vinci challenger
catalysts.description: CNBC feature frames Ottava as J&J's entry into a 'lucrative new market,' alongside Medtronic's Hugo continuing to add FDA-cleared indications (CNBC, MedTech Dive).

catalysts.title: Agility Robotics to go public via a $2.5B SPAC (ticker AGLT)
catalysts.description: Merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI expected to close by year-end, bringing $620M+ in cash including ~$200M from a Foxconn-led group; unveiled the next-gen Digit v5 humanoid alongside the deal (GeekWire).

catalysts.title: OpenAI confirms humanoid-robot hardware ambitions
catalysts.description: Sam Altman said infrastructure and manufacturing come before a personal home robot; the company has posted roughly 19 robotics roles covering actuators, firmware and prototyping.

catalysts.title: FANUC and Google ship an AI welding agent
catalysts.description: Built on Gemini Enterprise, the system converts engineering drawings directly into robot welding programs and motion paths; shipments targeted for December.

catalysts.title: Unitree's Shanghai debut closes up 460% (peaked +629% intraday)
catalysts.description: Valued the company near $66B at the open before a sustained slide — still the standout data point for how frothy humanoid sentiment can get in a single session (CNBC, Bloomberg).

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: Jetson Thor (Blackwell) modules are now shipping and NVIDIA opened an Isaac GR00T reference humanoid design to academic labs, extending its role as the default compute/software stack for Figure, Agility, Skild and others; also sits in your AI, Quantum and Biotech sleeves — don't triple-count the exposure.

positions.name: Rockwell Automation
positions.note: No fresh robotics-specific catalyst this week, but the $200B+ reshoring buildout thesis is intact and the Sep 15 Anthropic 'Project Glasswing' partnership adds an AI-security layer on top of the core automation business.

positions.name: Teradyne
positions.note: Universal Robots' Gen 7 cobot platform (PolyScope X) launched at IMTS Chicago on top of the robotics segment's first-ever $100M quarter — a real product cycle, not just a backlog story.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: 'Project Swarm' magnet-capacity reservations keep building ahead of the $1.3B Northlake, TX facility, underwriting the actuator/magnet supply chain every humanoid maker depends on; also counts against your Critical Minerals sleeve.

positions.name: AeroVironment
positions.note: Record $1.5B backlog (+37% YoY, 1.4x book-to-bill) with margins moving toward 40%; shares have already re-rated to ~$160, so some of the good news may be priced in. Also counts against your Defense sleeve.

positions.name: Symbotic
positions.note: Turned GAAP-profitable in Q2 FY26 ($9M net income vs a $10M loss a year ago) on $676M revenue (+23% YoY) and a ~$22.6B backlog, with Q3 guidance raised to $700–720M — upgrading from Speculative now that the profitability thesis is showing up in the numbers, sell-side target cuts notwithstanding.

positions.name: Vishay Precision Group
positions.note: Its analyst target nearly doubled to $77 on a humanoid-vendor sensor design win, but shares have since pulled back ~11% on customer-concentration concerns — real optionality, kept small.

positions.name: Harmonic Drive Systems
positions.note: Makes the dominant strain-wave gear reducers that sit at the humanoid-actuator bottleneck, but its order book hasn't yet shown the consistent quarter-to-quarter conversion that would justify a larger position.

positions.name: Kratos Defense
positions.note: Valkyrie drone and a growing laser-systems business delivered +30.5% Q2 revenue and a $2.08B backlog, but the autonomy piece is smaller and less proven than AeroVironment's — sized as optionality. Also counts against your Defense sleeve.

positions.name: Intuitive Surgical
positions.note: A fresh EU approval for da Vinci SP hasn't stopped shares from sitting ~34% off their highs as J&J's Ottava (a flattering CNBC feature this month) and Medtronic's Hugo (still adding FDA-cleared indications) both turn into credible, multi-system competitors.

positions.name: Cognex
positions.note: Raised its through-cycle EBITDA margin target to 25–31%, but the stock is still digesting an HSBC downgrade — good business, unresolved near-term sentiment.

positions.name: Caterpillar
positions.note: Formalized a FieldAI physical-AI partnership on Sep 5, but robotics/autonomy remains a rounding error against Caterpillar's core equipment revenue and the adoption pace outside mining is unproven.

positions.name: Deere & Company
positions.note: Continues rolling out autonomous 9RX tractors and an autonomous commercial mower, but Deere discloses no standalone autonomy revenue — a slow-burn option on future automation, not a name to size around today.

positions.name: Fanuc
positions.note: Q1 net profit was up 35% and the new FANUC/Google Gemini 'AI Welding Agent' (engineering drawings straight to robot programs, shipping customers in December) is a genuine AI-native product, but shares are still below the average analyst target with earnings due Oct 22.

positions.name: ABB
positions.note: Selling its Robotics division to SoftBank for a $5.375B enterprise value simplifies the story but also removes robotics as an ABB-specific thesis until the deal — still awaiting regulatory clearance, expected mid-to-late 2026 — actually closes.

positions.name: Serve Robotics
positions.note: Q2 revenue grew 404% to $3.2M on 792 daily active robots, but FY26 revenue guidance was cut to $9–10M from $26M in the same release — real growth, but small and now less predictable.

positions.name: Johnson & Johnson
positions.note: Ottava got a flattering CNBC profile this month as J&J's entry into surgical robotics, but the system is still pre-commercial and robotics is immaterial to J&J's overall P&L — a name to watch for the surgical-robotics thesis, not to hold for it.

positions.name: Tesla
positions.note: Optimus output has ramped roughly 10x from Q2 to several hundred units a week, but Tesla's own engineers describe the AI as unable to generalize past tightly supervised tasks, and Musk's 2025 promise of thousands of robots 'doing useful work' was walked back to zero as of January 2026 — this is a bet on Tesla's core business, not an investable robotics thesis on its own.

positions.name: Unitree Robotics
positions.note: The stock has given back most of its Shanghai IPO-day pop (peaked +629% intraday, closed +460%, valued near $66B at the open) even after the Sep 15 G1+ launch, and both a US FCC import ban and China's own NDRC bubble warning remain in force — plus there's no clean way for a US investor to hold STAR Market-listed shares directly.
